sources.text: European Commission - Daily News Daily News 14 / 10 / 2026 Brussels, 14 October 2026 Commission disburses close to €1 billion in RRF payments to Sweden and the Netherlands Today, the European Commission disbursed nearly €1 billion to Sweden and the Netherlands under the Recovery and Resilience Facility (RRF). The Facility is the centrepiece of NextGenerationEU – the Commission's post-pandemic programme to support Member States' recovery, economic growth, and competitiveness. Sweden received €333 million, marking its third and final payment under the RRF. The payment supports reforms and investments linked to the green transition and improvements in labour and housing markets. These include measures to strengthen the development and deployment of innovative industrial technologies with zero, low or negative greenhouse gas emissions; expand enrolment in higher education; and increase the supply of new energy-efficient rental housing. Sweden submitted its final payment request on 2 July 2026, which the Commission greenlighted on 31 August 2026 . Following a favourable opinion from the Council's Economic and Financial Committee and the Commission's payment decision, the funds have now been disbursed. With this final instalment, Sweden has received its full allocation of €3.45 billion, having fulfilled all milestones and targets in its national recovery and resilience plan. The Netherlands received €661 million, marking its fourth RRF payment. The measures linked to this disbursement include reforms such as the transition to a new pension system, as well as investments in offshore wind environmental protection, energy-saving home upgrades, green hydrogen research and demonstration projects, digital education solutions, and up- and reskilling for unemployed people. The Dutch authorities submitted their fourth payment request on 2 July 2026, which the Commission approved on 7 September 2026 . The funds were released after a favourable opinion from the Council's Economic and Financial Committee and the Commission's payment decision. Overall, the Netherlands' plan is financed by €5.44 billion in grants. With today's payment, total disbursements to the country reach 68.6% of its allocation, while 81.1% of the plan's milestones and targets have been completed. As with all Member States, RRF payments are performance-based and depend on the successful delivery of agreed reforms and investments. With the Facility due to close at the end of 2026, Member States had to complete all outstanding milestones and targets by August 2026 and submit final payment requests by the end of September. An interactive map showcasing examples of reforms and investments supported by the RRF is available online. Further details on the RRF payment claim process are also available online.

sources.text:
Commission disburses €2.86 billion to Ukraine for drones, missiles and urgent battlefield needs
Publication date: 14 October 2026

Today, the European Commission disbursed €2.86 billion to Ukraine under the defence component of the €90 billion Ukraine Support Loan . The funding will go towards drones, air defence systems, missiles, radars, electronic warfare systems and ammunitions .

Ursula von der Leyen , President of the European Commission, said: “As Russia stalls on the frontlines, it continues to escalate its aerial attacks - cruelly targeting Ukrainian civilians and infrastructure. Europe's steadfast support matters more than ever to help Ukraine protect its skies and save lives. With today's €2.86 billion disbursement, we keep addressing Ukraine's most urgent operational needs, including drones and missiles vital to its defence.”

The Ukraine Support Loan includes funding with an indicative split of €60 billion for defence and €30 billion for budgetary assistance over 2026–2027. In 2026 alone, €28.3 billion is planned for disbursement to support Ukraine's defence industrial capacity. Further disbursements under the 2026 defence leg of the instrument will continue in the coming weeks.

As Ukraine prepares for its fourth winter since Russia's full-scale invasion, the urgent delivery of defence equipment ensures that Ukraine's armed forces can protect their civilians and cities from Russian attacks.

All funding decisions respond to Ukraine's evolving needs and are subject to agreed conditions and monitoring. Since 2022, the EU and its Member States have provided €231.5 billion in overall support to Ukraine , including €3.8 billion from the proceeds of immobilised Russian assets.

For the rest of 2026, Ukraine still has €29.64 billion available in financial support . That includes €25.24 billion for disbursement under the Ukraine Support Loan, consisting of €12.54 billion to support Ukraine's defence industrial capacity and €12.7 billion in budget support. In addition, €4.4 billion in budget support is still available under the initial Ukraine Facility for this year. More than €17 billion in budget support is therefore available for the remaining months of 2026, subject to the fulfilment of the relevant conditions outlined in the Ukraine Plan and the Memorandum of Understanding.

Background

In February 2026, the European Parliament and the Council adopted Regulation (EU) 2026/467 , establishing the Ukraine Support Loan. The Regulation provides for up to €90 billion in support to Ukraine. The support is structured around two complementary components: assistance to strengthen Ukraine's defence capabilities and defence industrial capacities; and support to ensure the continued functioning of the state, maintain essential public services and strengthen economic resilience.

Following Ukraine's submission of its Financing Strategy in March 2026, the Council adopted, on 23 April 2026, an Implementing Decision determining the assistance to be made available to Ukraine in 2026.

The defence component focuses on reconstructing and modernising Ukraine's defence technological and industrial base, while supporting its gradual integration into the European defence technological and industrial base.

sources.text: Press release 21-10-2026 - 12:47 20261018IPR48259 Parliament backs storm recovery aid for Portugal, Spain, Italy and Malta On Wednesday, MEPs voted to unlock aid worth €489 million to help the four countries recover following severe storms and flooding earlier this year. The European Union Solidarity Fund (EUSF) aid, approved by 651 votes in favour, 17 against, and three abstentions, supports emergency and recovery operations. Malta and Italy requested help after storm Harry struck in January 2026; Portugal and Spain also did so after a series of storms caused severe flooding between January and February 2026. The breakdown of the funding is as follows: Portugal: €261.5 million (€65.37 million advance already received);• Spain: €149.1 million (€37.26 million advance already received); • Italy: €74.9 million; • Malta: €3.7 million (€931.014 advance already received). • The EUSF support helps finance emergency and recovery measures, such as restoring energy, water, wastewater, telecommunications and transport infrastructure, as well as to fund health and education services. The aid also covers clean-up operations, temporary accommodation and rescue services, and measures to secure preventive infrastructure and protect cultural heritage. Plenary notes that actions currently financed under the Solidarity Fund should continue to be adequately financed under the next EU long-term budget (MFF), to respond to the intensification of natural disasters and provide tangible support for the member states and regions affected. Since 2002, the EU Solidarity Fund has provided over €11 billion in aid in response to 150 disaster events, including 130 natural disasters and 20 health emergencies, across 25 member states (plus the UK) and six accession countries. The EUSF is part of the Solidarity and Emergency Aid Reserve, a special instrument of the EU budget, and its mobilisation has to be approved by both the Parliament and the Council.
